questions.enonce_markdown:
A square lamina $ABCD$ has side $4\ \mathrm{cm}$. A triangle $BCE$ with $EF = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$, where $F$ is the midpoint of $BC$, is cut off from the square. Find the distance of the centre of gravity of the remaining lamina $ABECD$ from the side $AD$.

![fig-1](gce-al-pm-mechanics-2026-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Set-up (from the figure).** $ABCD$ is the square with $AD$ the left-hand side and $BC$ the right-hand side. $F$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $EF = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$ is drawn perpendicular to $BC$, pointing into the square (the triangle $BCE$ is isosceles, $EB = EC$). Measure $x$ from the side $AD$ ($x = 0$ on $AD$, $x = 4$ on $BC$). The lamina is uniform, so weights are proportional to areas and the centre of gravity of each piece is its centroid.

| Piece | Area ($\mathrm{cm^2}$) | Distance of centroid from $AD$ ($\mathrm{cm}$) |
|---|---|---|
| Whole square $ABCD$ | $4\times 4 = 16$ | $2$ |
| Removed triangle $BCE$ | $\tfrac12\times 4\times 3 = 6$ | $4 - \tfrac13(3) = 3$ |
| Remaining lamina $ABECD$ | $16 - 6 = 10$ | $\bar{x}$ |

The centroid of a triangle lies one third of the way from the base along the median, so the centroid of $BCE$ is $\tfrac13 EF = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$ from $BC$, that is $4 - 1 = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$ from $AD$ (check: $\tfrac13(4 + 4 + 1) = 3$, since $E$ is $1\ \mathrm{cm}$ from $AD$).

**Moments about $AD$** (square = remaining lamina + triangle):

$$16\times 2 = 10\,\bar{x} + 6\times 3$$

$$10\,\bar{x} = 32 - 18 = 14 \;\Rightarrow\; \bar{x} = 1.4$$

**The centre of gravity of the lamina $ABECD$ is $1.4\ \mathrm{cm}$ from $AD$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ move with constant velocities $(2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $(-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively at time $t$ seconds. Initially, $P$ and $Q$ are at points with position vectors $(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m}$ and $(\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m}$ respectively. Write down the equation of the path of each particle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For constant velocity $\mathbf{v}$ from the initial position $\mathbf{r}_0$, the position at time $t$ is $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{v}t$.

**Particle $P$:**

$$\mathbf{r}_P = (\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) + t(2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) = (1 + 2t)\mathbf{i} + (-1 + 3t)\mathbf{j}\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Particle $Q$:**

$$\mathbf{r}_Q = (\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) + t(-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}) = (1 - t)\mathbf{i} + (3 + 4t)\mathbf{j}\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Cartesian form of each path** (eliminate $t$ from $x$ and $y$): for $P$, $x = 1 + 2t$ and $y = -1 + 3t$ give $3x - 2y = 5$; for $Q$, $x = 1 - t$ and $y = 3 + 4t$ give $4x + y = 7$. Both paths are straight lines.

**Paths: $\mathbf{r}_P = (\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) + t(2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})$ (that is $3x - 2y = 5$) and $\mathbf{r}_Q = (\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) + t(-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})$ (that is $4x + y = 7$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two particles $P$ and $Q$ move with constant velocities $(2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $(-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively at time $t$ seconds. Initially, $P$ and $Q$ are at points with position vectors $(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m}$ and $(\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{m}$ respectively. Calculate the distance between $P$ and $Q$ when $t = 1$ second.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Positions at $t = 1$** (from part (a)):

$$\mathbf{r}_P = (1 + 2)\mathbf{i} + (-1 + 3)\mathbf{j} = 3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$$

$$\mathbf{r}_Q = (1 - 1)\mathbf{i} + (3 + 4)\mathbf{j} = 7\mathbf{j}$$

**Displacement from $P$ to $Q$:**

$$\overrightarrow{PQ} = \mathbf{r}_Q - \mathbf{r}_P = -3\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}$$

**Distance:**

$$PQ = \sqrt{(-3)^{2} + 5^{2}} = \sqrt{34} \approx 5.83\ \mathrm{m}$$

(Alternatively, the relative position is $\mathbf{r}_Q - \mathbf{r}_P = (0\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}) + t(-3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j})$, which at $t = 1$ is $-3\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}$.)

**The distance between $P$ and $Q$ at $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$ is $\sqrt{34} \approx 5.83\ \mathrm{m}$.**
